z_probe.derivation: Observed in the machine's own configfile, not in any manual. `[homing_override]` runs `G1 X{km.print_max[0]/2} Y{km.print_max[1]/2} F12000` immediately before `G28.6245197 Z`, and `_km_globals.print_max` reads [390, 390] on the live machine — so Z is probed at the centre of the bed. The chain is `G28` -> `[gcode_macro g28]` -> `LAZY_HOME` -> `G28.6245197 X Y Z` -> `[homing_override]`. Note two inert variants that look like they home but do not: `[homing_override]` only branches on (X and Y and Z) or (X and Y and not Z), so `G28 Z` and `G28 X` alone fall through both branches and home nothing at all.

probe_operations.what: Homes Z by touching the bed at one point.
probe_operations.derivation: [homing_override] drives to G1 X{print_max[0]/2} Y{print_max[1]/2} immediately before G28.6245197 Z; _km_globals.print_max reads [390,390] live.

probe_operations.what: Levels the two Z motors by probing one point near each side.
probe_operations.derivation: [z_tilt] points = 15,202.5 and 375,202.5 in the machine's own configfile.

probe_operations.what: Runs KAMP's adaptive BED_MESH_CALIBRATE, which fits its mesh to the bounding box of the objects being printed and probes a grid across it. On a resume those objects ARE the part already standing on the bed, so this walks a grid straight onto it. This is the widest-reaching probe on the machine and the spec did not have it.
probe_operations.derivation: [gcode_macro g29] runs G28 then BED_MESH_CALIBRATE PROFILE=kamp because _km_globals.bedmesh_before_print = 1. [gcode_macro BED_MESH_CALIBRATE] takes the min/max of printer.exclude_object.objects polygons, grows them by _KAMP_Settings.mesh_margin (5, fuzz_amount 0), enforces a minimum of twice the default probe spacing, and clamps to bed_mesh mesh_min 15,15 / mesh_max 375,375 (probe_count 9,9 -> 45 mm spacing -> 90 mm minimum region). With no objects declared it says so on the console and meshes the full clamp rectangle.

probe_operations.what: Touches the bed wherever the toolhead is standing; the vendor start block issues it after G0 Y1.
probe_operations.derivation: Observed on the machine's console during a print: `// probe at 195.000,0.999 is z=0.109531`, immediately following the start block's `G0 Y1`.

INIT_MAPPING_VALUE.reason: Binds tool indices to physical filament slots. Without it the machine keeps whatever binding the previous print left behind.
INIT_MAPPING_VALUE.proof: Running it flipped `value_t0` in save_variables from `slot2` to `slot0`. Negative evidence from the same evening: with the line deleted, a print that asked for slot 1 fed from slot 3.

BOX_PRINT_START.reason: Loads filament from the bound slot into the hotend. Manual loading is not required precisely because this line does it.
BOX_PRINT_START.proof: Absent from `/printer/gcode/help` yet demonstrably works — it is registered by a compiled module, not a config macro. Its effect is observable as filament reaching the nozzle with no manual load step.

filament_detected.means: State of the filament switch. Carries no information while the sensor is disabled: observed live reading `filament_detected: true` with `enabled: false` on a machine mid-print.

filament_used.means: Sum of commanded E movement in millimetres. It is what the extruder was told to do, not what reached the nozzle, so it keeps counting through a jam or a stripped filament.

print_duration.means: Wall-clock since the start block began, which includes purge, Z-tilt and a full 9x9 bed mesh. It is already running long before the first layer, so an idle detector built on it raises a false alarm during legitimate probing.

print_stats.info.current_layer.valid_when: the G-code has been post-processed to emit SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO CURRENT_LAYER
print_stats.info.current_layer.means: Whatever the last CURRENT_LAYER command set. The slicer emits only TOTAL_LAYER, so on unprocessed G-code this stays 0 for the whole print and a stalled job looks identical to a healthy one. Reading 0 is ambiguous in a second way that cost time to untangle: it also reads 0 on a correctly processed file for as long as the start block is running, which on this machine is a Z-tilt plus a full 9x9 bed mesh and takes over ten minutes. A 0 means 'no layer has begun' — not 'this file lacks the command'. Tell the two apart by TOTAL_LAYER being set (the start block has run) together with print_duration still climbing, or by looking in the file.

print_stats.message.means: Empty for vendor error codes. `QDE_004_006 Extruder loading failure` appears only in the console ring buffer at /server/gcode_store, which overwrites within minutes.

webcam_snapshot.means: A JPEG from /webcam/?action=snapshot on port 80 — not on the API port 7125, which answers that path with a JSON 404 that reads like a camera fault. The camera returns a perfectly valid HTTP 200 and a well-formed 1920x1080 JPEG with the chamber light off; it is simply black. Measured: 50306 bytes of essentially-black frame while `output_pin caselight` read 0. So a frame arriving is not evidence that the print can be seen. The light follows the screen on this machine — the console shows `[smart_output_pin caselight] SCREEN=..., PRINT=standby -> LIGHT=`, so it goes out when the panel sleeps, with no print-side cause at all. The spec's separate caveat still stands on top of this one: on a small part in the middle of the bed the head blocks the view even when lit.
